result.title: 1. Introduction
result.summary: FPIF, an Illinois-created fund governed by a nine-member Board under the Pension Code, manages investments for about 300 local firefighter pension funds; it held approximately $7.6 billion as of January 2023. This RFP seeks a non-discretionary private-markets consultant and three discretionary OCIO advisors. Respondents must obtain forms online and monitor FPIF’s website for updates. Target allocations are 10% private equity, 7% private debt, 10% real estate, and 4% infrastructure. The consultant oversees 3%, 2%, 5%, and 2%, respectively; discretionary mandates divide the remainder among private equity (4% PE advisor; 3% opportunistic), real assets (2.5% debt, 5% real estate, 2% infrastructure), and opportunistic strategies (2.5% debt). Requirements cover sourcing and investing across buyouts, growth, venture, secondaries, co-investments, core and non-core real assets, and diverse credit strategies, with specified experience, performance, access, and portfolio-construction expectations. FPIF seeks diversified, return-oriented solutions, may retain veto rights, and prefers separate accounts except potentially venture fund-of-funds. Illinois law also encourages vendor fiduciary diversity.

result.title: 2. Proposal Content
key_items: 2.3. Minimum Qualifications Certification; 2.4. Description of Respondent’s Experience and Qualifications; 2.5. References; 2.6. Fee Proposal; 2.7 Additional Documentation and Data
2.4. Description of Respondent’s Experience and Qualifications
result.summary: Proposals must address every Section 2 requirement in separate sections, preferably in a zip file with a table of contents; noncompliant formatting may lead to rejection. Include a signed business-letter cover letter from an authorized representative, identifying their title and authority. It must affirm compliance, truthfulness and completeness, offer validity through 360 days after the deadline, disclose specified relationships or negotiations, acknowledge possible public disclosure, identify all proposal documents, certify no fraud, collusion, or related remuneration, and accept Exhibit A certifications and terms. Complete Exhibit B questions in order, repeating each question and number and answering fully without cross-references; complete Exhibit C minimum-qualification certification. Describe consulting experience, firmwide and proposed-class AUM/AUA, investment inception dates, lead consultant/CIO experience, subcontracted services and oversight, and team roles. Provide three references, including a public defined-benefit plan, with contact details; FPIF may contact them. Submit Exhibit D all-inclusive fees and Exhibit E documentation. Address FOIA disclosure by labeling confidential pages, identifying applicable exemptions and justifications, and flagging confidentiality in the submission email; FPIF decides confidentiality.

result.title: 3. Timeline and Submission Requirements
result.summary: The procurement timeline is subject to FPIF’s discretion; updates will be posted on its website, which respondents must check. Key dates: RFP issued February 13, 2023; questions due February 24 by noon Central; answers posted March 3; proposals due March 10 by noon Central; possible interviews in Q2 or Q3 2023 and presentations in Q3 or Q4; anticipated consultant selection May 26 and discretionary-advisor selection August 25. Proposals must follow the RFP and be emailed as PDFs by the deadline to Mitchell Green (mgreen@ifpif.org) and investments@ifpif.org. No other submission method is accepted; late proposals may be rejected. Use the specified subject line, “Response to FPIF Private Markets Consulting and Advisory RFP – (Name of Respondent),” or risk rejection. FPIF will confirm receipt. Proposals may be withdrawn before the deadline by signed written notice received by then, referencing the RFP and respondent; they may be resubmitted with modifications by the deadline. Other modification methods are not accepted, and withdrawals are confirmed by email.

result.title: 4. Procurement Rules and Procedure
key_items: 4.1. Procurement Rules; 4.2. Communications; Quiet Period; 4.3. Procurement Contact
result.summary: FPIF’s Board-adopted procurement rules and applicable law govern the process, overseen by staff and advisors; FPIF will publish the selected respondent, contract amount, fees, and selection factors. A quiet period runs from RFP issuance until selection or process completion, barring procurement-related ex parte contact and improper influence (with a limited exception for ordinary, unrelated work with existing providers); violations may cause disqualification. Questions must go to Procurement Contact Mitchell Green by the stated deadline and will be answered anonymously in a consolidated website Q&A. Proposals are checked for completeness, accuracy, and compliance, then assessed for best value using factors including experience, mandate fit, assets, team and stability, investment and sourcing capabilities, performance, risk, DEI/ESG, clients, pricing, ethics, references, location, and qualifying ownership status. FPIF may seek clarification or evidence but generally bars post-deadline changes. Submissions become FPIF property and may be publicly disclosed; respondents bear costs. FPIF reserves broad rights to change, waive, supplement, negotiate, cancel, reject, or disqualify.

result.title: Exhibit A: Certifications and Terms Required by State Law
result.summary: Exhibit A lists 27 Illinois-law certifications and contract terms required of FPIF respondents; anyone unable to comply must explain the numbered item and reason in their proposal. Requirements cover ethics; bribery, securities felonies, state debt, use tax, environmental and lead-poisoning violations; conflicts, financial interests and political contributions; drug-free workplaces, bid rigging, international boycotts, third-party fees, revolving-door rules and business registration; reporting anticompetitive conduct; nondiscrimination, affirmative action, sexual-harassment policies, discriminatory-club fees and prevailing wages. They also require seven-year transition-record retention and audit access, notice of employee-solicitation plans, and acknowledgment of open-meetings and public-records laws. Respondents must represent they are not specified Illinois-regulated finance entities; annually disclose workforce diversity and qualifying service contracts; disclose ownership and executives; and identify subcontractors, including marketers, their addresses and expected compensation, with written notice of changes. False certifications may void agreements where specified.

result.title: Exhibit B: Questionnaire
result.summary: Exhibit B is an FPIF proposal questionnaire requiring ordered questions and answers. It collects respondent contact, company, entity, ownership, control, and executive information; firm history, leadership, structure, offices, staffing, registrations, services, strategies, assets, clients, growth plans, revenue, ownership diversity, and certifications; and client wins/losses, public-fund engagements, conflicts, Illinois pension work, ESG/CSR policies, legal and regulatory matters, examinations, audits, continuity, cybersecurity, breaches, insurance, and ethics issues. It asks about workforce diversity, proposed and support teams, biographies, responsibilities, workload, compensation, stability, turnover, succession, client service, public-office roles, compliance leadership, and legal support. Detailed private equity, private debt, real estate, and infrastructure questions cover investment approaches, sourcing, due diligence, risk, allocations, GP relationships, market outlook, competition, fees, manager access, and performance. Templates request fund- and strategy-level capital, valuation, and return metrics. Further questions address capacity, comparable mandates, account minimums, reporting, software, attribution, GP financial-data reconciliation, fee monitoring, competitive advantages, and suitability as an FPIF partner.

nodes.title: Respondent Contact, Company, and Ownership Questionnaire
nodes.summary: Exhibit B requires the completed questionnaire to accompany the proposal, with responses in the listed order and each question followed by its answer. It collects company name, mailing address, state, ZIP code, city, phone, website, fax, and certified Federal Employer Identification Number, as well as the contractor’s applicable business entity type. It requests contact-person name, title, phone, fax, and email. Ownership information includes applicable entity classifications and, under Section 1-113.14(c) of the Pension Code, names and addresses of parent or controlling-interest entities, subsidiaries or entities controlled by the respondent, people with more than a 7.5% ownership or distributive-income share, and executive officers.

nodes.title: Organization
nodes.summary: An FPIF RFP questionnaire asks respondents to identify the contracting entity and proposed mandates; describe the firm’s founding, history, leadership, succession, strategy, institutional consulting/advisory experience, offices, staffing, Illinois presence, SEC registration, organizational structure, and anticipated changes. It requests current and historical AUA/AUM by asset class, private-market category, mandate type, and client type, plus client counts, commitments, uncalled capital, products, and services. Respondents must explain advisory approaches and differences between discretionary and non-discretionary work, access to oversubscribed funds, and success with first- or second-fund top-quartile managers. It also seeks client wins and losses, public-fund client details, growth plans, other business lines and revenue contributions, ownership structure and changes, and minority, women, disability ownership and MWDBE/Illinois business certifications.

nodes.title: Firm Client Firm Private Market Count (#) AUA/AUM ($) AUA/AUM ($)
nodes.summary: The RFP asks about the firm’s private-market products and services, advisory approach, access to high-demand funds, and experience identifying top-quartile emerging managers. It requests AUA/AUM by client type and private-market assets, explanations of “other,” and five-year client wins/losses with mandate and service dates; public-fund clients and service history; and three-to-five-year growth plans. It also covers other business lines and revenue, ownership and ownership changes, MWDBE status and ownership/workforce diversity, and diversity policies. Operational questions address business continuity and disaster recovery, physical and cybersecurity safeguards, breaches and third-party assessments, and professional-liability insurance. The firm must disclose any opposition to FPIF or Illinois Public Act 101-0610, Illinois Article 3/4 pension-fund engagements as of two dates, and potential conflicts. Further requests concern ESG/CSR policies and UNPRI status; legal proceedings and regulatory discipline; SEC examination findings and responses; and the current auditor and date of the last change.

nodes.title: Team
nodes.summary: The questions cover firm-wide and investment-professional headcounts; workforce diversity; staffing by private equity, debt, infrastructure, and real estate; research-team structure; and the proposed mandate’s leads, supporting personnel, biographies, experience, client loads, meeting attendance, contact details, team size, market coverage, and organizational chart. They ask how team stability is maintained, whether analysts specialize or generalize, how staff are evaluated and compensated, whether pay is tied to results, and how employee investments align interests. The firm must disclose overall and senior turnover, investment-professional departures since 2018, leadership and research departures or additions over ten years, circumstances, planned departures, and succession and retirement plans. The questions also cover client-service personnel, biographies, contact information, and work locations; employee public-office candidacies or service as investment-fund trustees; the Chief Compliance Officer and biography; and whether legal support is in-house or external, including counsel firms.

nodes.title: Strategy, Process, and Performance
nodes.summary: The RFP requests detailed information on proposed private equity and private debt advisory or consulting solutions. For private equity, it asks about experience, investment universe and strategy biases, buyout, growth, venture, niche-market, co-investment and secondary capabilities; risk management, philosophy, sourcing, GP selection, due diligence, macro integration, staffing, relationships, commitments, fund allocations and allocation policy. It also covers proprietary funds, market outlook, competitive advantages and competitors, fee mitigation, strategy return dispersion, top-manager access, manager databases, screening deliverables, and historical performance for specified strategy composites and benchmarks, with fund-level metrics and results through June 30, 2022. For private debt, it requests parallel information on experience, investment universe, strategy and debt-segment expertise, niche and dislocated-market sourcing, risk management, proprietary funds, philosophy, due diligence, commitments and allocation policies, staffing, GP relationships, market outlook, competitive position, fees, return dispersion, manager access, and representative or flagship performance.

nodes.title: June 30, 2022.
nodes.summary: The excerpt begins with a June 30, 2022 performance-table template, including fund size, investments, committed and invested capital, realized proceeds, unrealized and total value, vintage, and return metrics such as IRR, DPI, RVPI, TVPI, and MOIC, with a Private Debt Composite label. It then presents FPIF RFP questions for real assets advisers. Topics include experience and assets managed in core/non-core real estate and infrastructure; investable-universe biases and preferred strategies; core/non-core allocation advice; risk management, investment philosophy, macro and public-market influences, and GP selection; investment, operational, and legal due diligence; five-year commitments, fund counts, oversubscriptions, and capacity allocation; sourcing, staffing, GP relationships, fund history, and LPAC participation; market outlook and infrastructure attributes; strategy evaluation priorities; competitive advantages and competitors; fee mitigation; access to highly ranked managers; and flagship or representative composite performance.

nodes.title: June 30, 2022.
nodes.summary: Dated June 30, 2022, this FPIF RFP Exhibit B1 requests, if available, separate Core and Non-Core Real Estate and Infrastructure composite tables. For each composite, report fund and investment details, committed and invested capital, fund size, investment count, realized proceeds, unrealized and total value, gross/net MOIC and IRR, and DPI, RVPI, and TVPI. A second strategy-level table requests since-inception committed capital, fund count, and 1-, 3-, 5-, and 10-year and since-inception IRRs. Question 56 asks about asset-class capacity constraints and policies limiting AUM in proposed mandates. Question 57 requests the sizes and inception dates of the five largest mandates from unique investors with substantially similar Consulting and/or Advisory mandates as of December 31, 2022, plus the firm’s largest, smallest, average, and median client sizes.

nodes.title: Operations
nodes.summary: The section asks whether strategies are available through separately managed accounts and whether minimum account sizes apply; expected quarterly and annual reporting timelines; any significant compliance or ethics violations and how they were addressed; the firm’s competitive advantages and reasons to select it; client software and tools for reporting, sourcing, and evaluating strategies; and a sample quarterly report. It also requests details on private-markets attribution by asset class and manager, including online availability, and GP financial reporting and reconciliation procedures for valuations, commitments, paid-in and invested capital, distributions, expenses, management fees, and cash, including reconciliation with client custodians. Finally, it asks about fee-monitoring and validation services and any remarks on the firm’s unique suitability as an FPIF partner.

result.title: Exhibit C: Minimum Qualifications Certification
result.summary: Exhibit C is a minimum-qualifications certification to be completed, signed, and submitted with the proposal. The respondent certifies that it is a registered investment adviser or identifies its exemption; will serve as a fiduciary under the Illinois Pension Code if retained; and has all required legal authorizations. It must have a senior account lead with at least 10 years’ industry experience, at least $500 million in assets under management and five years of performance history in the proposed asset classes, experience managing investments for tax-exempt or governmental defined benefit plans, and at least 10 years of operation as an investment management organization, measured as of December 31, 2022. The form provides fields for the company, authorized signer’s name and title, signature, and date. Respondents that do not meet every minimum requirement should not submit a proposal to FPIF.

result.title: Exhibit D: Form of Fee Proposal
result.summary:

Please provide a fee proposal for the proposed mandate(s). Consultants should propose a flat annual fee structure for private markets consulting. Consultants that offer both general consulting and private market consulting should also submit a joint fee proposal for both services. Discretionary Advisors should propose a flat fee or asset-based management fee. Incentive compensation will be considered.

result.title: Exhibit E: Additional Documentation and Data
result.summary: Exhibit E requires respondents to attach all documents requested in Exhibit B and provide: ADV Part II; allocation policy; biographies of consultants, account leads, proposed senior personnel, and the Chief Compliance Officer; investment, operational, and legal due-diligence checklist documents; code of ethics or professional conduct; corporate social responsibility and diversity policies; disaster recovery and business continuity plans; a pitchbook or standard marketing presentation for proposed strategies; proof of E&O, professional liability, fiduciary, and other insurance coverage; a sample quarterly investment performance report; SEC review findings letter; sustainability and/or ESG policy; and, if applicable, state or local minority certification/registration and a GIPS verification letter.
